podcast.title: Mutation with Heavy Metal (1985)
podcast.body: By 1985, the original skate punk sound began incorporating heavy metal elements, particularly guitar solos. This evolution fractured the community; some bands transitioned to metal genres, while others remained dedicated to hardcore punk. "By 1985, the original Skate Punk sound had acquired a new thing, elements of heavy metal, including guitar solos."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Glory Years (Late 1994-2004)
podcast.body: The "glory years" of skate punk began in late 1994 and continued for approximately ten years, with The Offspring's success leading to wider discovery of bands like Goldfinger, Lagwagon, Face to Face, MXPX, and Unwritten Law. "Skate Punk's glory years began in late 1994 and continued for a good 10 years."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Coined by Thrasher Magazine
podcast.body: The term "Skate Punk" itself appears to have been coined by an employee of Thrasher Magazine. "The term Skate Punk also seems to have been coined by an employee of Thrasher Magazine."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Definition and Origins
podcast.body: Skate punk is a subgenre of Alt Rock built on skateboarding culture, with its roots tracing back to the shared music of surfers and skaters, and later evolving with punk rock in the late 1970s. Its "ground zero" is likely Oxnard, California. "My main interest with skateboarding is the music that evolved along with it."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early 2010s Resurgence
podcast.body: The early 2010s saw another surge in skateboarding's popularity, which in turn inspired a new generation of bands drawing from older skate punk groups. "In the early 2010s, there was another spike in popularity of skateboarding. And that resulted in a new crop of bands all inspired by older skate punk groups."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Sound and Issues
podcast.body: The early days of skate punk were characterized by sharp, fast, angry songs filled with adrenaline. While cathartic, this sound was also associated with problems like violence, including LA gang violence, which made playing gigs difficult for the skate crowd for a time. "As you heard, the early days of the genre were dominated by sharp, fast, angry songs, containing the maximum amount of adrenaline."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Hardcore Influence
podcast.body: Skate punk is listed as one of the genres that has been significantly influenced by hardcore music since the 1980s. "we've seen the influence this music has had on metal and in creating post-hardcore music as well as skate punk and emo."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Mainstream Breakthrough (1990s)
podcast.body: Skate punk experienced a significant mainstream breakthrough in the 1990s, especially after the rise of grunge and alt-rock. This was exemplified by bands like Pennywise with "Unknown Road" (1993) and No FX with "Punk in Drublic" (early 90s), culminating in The Offspring's "Smash" (1994) which brought the genre widespread recognition. "Skate Punk did have to wait for its turn for a mainstream breakthrough, but when it happened, it happened big."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Nardcore Scene
podcast.body: The Nardcore scene, named after Oxnard, California, emerged when local skaters formed bands like Aggression and Ill Repute, specializing in music for the skate crowd. "And the scene even had a name, Nardcore, after Oxnard."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: New Millennium Growth
podcast.body: By the new millennium, skate punk had become massive, with established bands like Blink-182, The Offspring, MXPX, Pennywise, and No FX thriving, and newer bands like Sum 41 emerging. "By the new millennium, skate punk was massive."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Origin of Term
podcast.body: The original name for skateboarding was "Sidewalk Surfing," illustrating a natural connection that allowed the surf sound and attitude to transition into skateboarding and skate punk music. "Overall, the original name of skateboarding was Sidewalk Surfing."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Surprising History of Surf Music

podcast.title: Original Name: Skate Thrash
podcast.body: The genre's original name was "Skate Thrash," which is related to the name of Thrasher Magazine. "The magazine's name is also related to the genre's original name, Skate Thrash."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Origins in Hardcore
podcast.body: Skate punk emerged with roots in California hardcore, as demonstrated by early bands like Suicidal Tendencies. "and bits of skate punk."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Shift to Melodic Sound
podcast.body: Skate punk bands began to integrate more melodic elements, retaining their fast and intense qualities but adding "singable melodies." Bad Religion's 1988 album "Suffer" is seen as a key inflection point for this shift towards "pop sensibilities." "Some Skate Punk bands started to get more melodic."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
